items.archaeology: 50aafdce 'fix(db-base): extend withRetry to catch mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT with lossless heal', a5c449df 'fix(db-base): address review feedback — rename, integrity check, BUSY retry', 8a1607e9 'fix(db-base): use prepare().get() for quick_check to avoid pragma() type mismatch' — three-commit chain, same day (2026-06-23), shows mid-session corruption self-heal is a real, iterated-on feature in v1, not a one-off patch. ORIGINAL_INTENT (50aafdce): catch mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT and heal losslessly rather than fail hard.
items.regressions: REGRESSION_RISK (blocker): ADR P1 says 'no fallback chains' / hard deny. If v2 removes mid-session self-heal per P1 without a replacement, every mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT that #867's three commits now catch and heal will instead hard-fail the session. That is a direct v1-behavior regression unless the hard-error path is accepted as the intended v2 trade-off.
items.question: Is dropping mid-session lossless heal (replacing it with hard-error + doctor) an accepted trade-off of P1, or an unintended loss of the #867/50aafdce fix?
items.recommendation: State explicitly in an ADR that P1 knowingly removes mid-session self-heal (trading resilience for simplicity) rather than leaving it as an open question — the three-commit history shows this heal code took real engineering effort and silently dropping it should be a named decision, not a byproduct of P1.

summary: 21 rows reviewed (I3 second half). No cases found where r2's verdict is provably wrong. Strongest findings: #867 mid-session self-heal is a real, 3-commit-deep v1 fix that P1 would silently remove — needs an explicit ADR trade-off statement, not silence. #865 CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR handling has recurred 4 times across subsystems; v2 needs one resolver, not per-subsystem fixes. #889 tarball hygiene already has a working v1 test (f9c8d864) that must be carried forward when D2 removes scripts. #880's live-PID cleanup race needs an explicit check-inside-transaction design, not a restated single-writer rule. #878's fix chain (6f699fac/a11f313b) modeled plain-text chunking on markdown chunking's cap — if markdown chunking's oversized-single-paragraph gap (the actual #878 bug) is still open, the plain-text fix inherited a flawed assumption; needs direct re-test. #901's doctor/upgrade path mismatch already recurred once for Codex (#771) and needs a generic one-resolver rule, not a per-adapter patch, to avoid a third recurrence.
